## Context / Problem

`docs/plan-review-gate.md` (~lines 534-540) states a bug is NOT exempt from
plan review in general -- it gets a light advisory-only tier -- while
`src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:45`'s `_PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES` makes `bug`
exempt from the CLAIM-time gate specifically. Lines 1577-1578 and 1598
clarify these are separate axes ("The claim-time exemption is untouched"),
but the guide never states the operational SEQUENCE an author should
follow: claim a bug without plan review to perform root-cause analysis
(RCA) first, then -- once RCA yields an implementation plan and file
impact for a complex remediation -- get that plan LLM-reviewed before
implementation begins. Absent that explicit sequence, the two true (and
non-contradictory) statements read as if a bug is either always exempt or
never exempt, depending which passage is read.

## Approach

Correct the maintained guide directly at the claim-time-exemption /
bug-tier passage (~lines 534-540, 1577-1578, 1598). State the sequence
explicitly: a bug may be claimed without plan review to perform RCA; after
RCA, a complex bug with an implementation plan and recorded file impact
must receive LLM plan review (an explicit review-plan run on the bug,
which yields a real -- non-exempt -- verdict per the existing bug tier /
blast-radius escalation) before remediation begins. Preserve the existing
behavioral code/tests (gates.py, the bug review tier, blast-radius
escalation) as authority; do not change their behavior.

## Scope

- `docs/plan-review-gate.md`
- `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py` and `tests/unit/test_bug_review_tier.py`
  as behavior evidence/checks (read-only verification, not behavior
  changes)

## Testing

Run focused bug-review tier tests and add/update a documentation
assertion that distinguishes claim-time exemption (CLI, always) from
implementation-time plan review (LLM, required post-RCA for complex
bugs).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The guide states a bug may be claimed without plan review
      specifically to perform RCA.
- [ ] The guide states a complex bug -- one with an implementation plan
      and recorded file impact after RCA -- must receive LLM plan review
      before implementation begins.
- [ ] The guide does not imply every bug needs review before claim, nor
      that complex-bug remediation is permanently exempt from LLM review.
- [ ] Focused bug-review tier tests and a new documentation-content check
      pass.
